title: Emails, WhatsApp replies and letters that win trust

say: Emails, WhatsApp replies and business letters that win trust.
This is the video for module 2 of Business Communication.
Email is still the main formal channel for banks, grant programmes, larger companies and government. Your email is often the first thing they see of your business.

say: WhatsApp is often your shop window, your order book and your customer service desk, all in one. Customers decide in seconds whether you are serious.

say: And a formal letter is still needed when you apply for a contract, make a complaint or confirm an agreement.

say: Start with a specific subject line. Hello tells the reader nothing. Request for invoice, Main Hall booking, 29 March, tells them everything before they open it.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Then the body has five parts. First, the greeting. Dear Mrs Okoro for formal, or Good morning Tunde for a known contact.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Second, one sentence saying why you are writing.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Third, only the details the reader needs, in short paragraphs or a list.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Fourth, a clear request: what you want and by when, ideally as a question.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Fifth, your signature: full name, role, business name and phone number. Mention and clearly name every attachment.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email

say: Put the person who must act in the To line, and people who only need to know in CC.
When you email many customers who do not know each other, use BCC, so their addresses stay private.

panel.heading: The five parts of a business email
panel.rule: To is for action. CC is for information. BCC keeps addresses private.

say: For example, Ngozi runs a small catering business in Lagos. She emails Mrs Adebayo at a logistics company.
Her purpose sentence names who referred her and what it is about.

panel.heading: Ngozi's email to a corporate client

cards.d: Mr Kola Ojo of your HR team suggested I contact you about lunch packs for staff training days.
Packed lunches for groups of 20 to 150, about 3,500 naira per pack. Menu and price list attached.
Could we arrange a free tasting for two of your team next week? Tuesday or Thursday afternoon.

say: Her details are short: groups of 20 to 150, about 3,500 naira per pack at current prices, with the menu attached as one PDF.

say: Her request is a clear question with two days to choose from. When she got no reply, she followed up politely in the same email thread.

say: Most customers ask the same things. Is it available? How much? How do I pay? When can I get it?
A complete reply greets them by name and confirms it is available.

panel.heading: A complete customer reply

say: It gives the price and options, explains payment and delivery, and ends with one clear question.
Every extra message you make a customer send is a chance for them to buy elsewhere.

panel.heading: A complete customer reply

say: A new customer asks how much the blue necklace is. Halima used to reply, 8k. Then the customer had to ask everything else, and often left.

Now she replies completely. Yes, it is available. It is 8,000 naira. Matching earrings are 3,000 extra. Delivery within Abuja is about 2,000 naira and takes 1 to 2 days, paid by bank transfer. Would you like the earrings too?
The customer says yes, and Halima confirms in writing: a total of 13,000 naira, and asks for the delivery address.
Always confirm every order in one written message with items, total, payment and delivery date.
Before you deliver, check the payment in your own banking app or the SMS alert from your bank.

say: For example, Grace owns a printing shop in Enugu. Her new generator stopped working after two weeks.
Her first letter was angry, with no date, no receipt number and no clear request.

panel.heading: Grace's complaint letter

say: Her new letter, in full block format, names the generator and receipt number, says what happened, and asks for repair or replacement by 28 March.
She closes Yours faithfully, because she opened with Dear Sir or Madam. If you open with a name, close with Yours sincerely.

panel.heading: Grace's complaint letter

say: To remember. Write a specific subject line, and follow the five parts of an email.
Give complete WhatsApp replies, confirm orders in writing, and check payments yourself.
For complaints, give facts, evidence, a fair request and a deadline.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A specific subject line is the first step to a reply
One complete WhatsApp reply, then a written summary
Check payments in your own bank app
Complaints: facts, evidence, fair request, deadline
